what_it_does: A point cloud is a 3D scan of the real world represented as millions of scattered coordinate points — think of the output of a self-driving car's LIDAR sensor. Processing point clouds with custom hardware is hard because the points are irregularly scattered, so you cannot predict in advance which points will need to be compared with which neighbors, making it difficult to keep data on the fast on-chip memory (a small, fast scratchpad called SRAM) rather than repeatedly fetching it from the slower off-chip memory chips (DRAM). StreamGrid solves this by forcing the point cloud to be divided into a regular grid of fixed-size cells ('compulsory splitting'), which guarantees that the working data for each cell fits on-chip; a second technique ('deterministic termination') lets the hardware know exactly when it is done with each cell so it can safely flush results and accept new data without stalling. Together, these two ideas make point cloud processing amenable to the streaming pipeline style that is already efficient for image processing.
